faq.title: What does 'IMS Status: Unregistered' mean on Android?
faq.description: IMS (IP Multimedia Subsystem) is the core cellular framework that routes voice calls as packet data over LTE and 5G networks. If your IMS Status displays 'Unregistered', your carrier has not authorized your device for packet voice, or your APN configuration is missing the 'ims' bearer tag. Consequently, your phone cannot make VoLTE or Wi-Fi calls.

faq.title: How do I check my phone's hidden IMS Registration status?
faq.description: Open your Phone dialer app and enter: *#*#4636#*#*. In the hidden Testing menu, tap 'Phone information', tap the three-dot menu icon in the top right, and select 'IMS Service Status'. A dialogue will display whether IMS, VoLTE, VoWiFi, and Video Calling are 'Registered' or 'Unregistered'.

faq.title: Why does Wi-Fi Calling (VoWiFi) fail even when connected to strong home Wi-Fi?
faq.description: VoWiFi requires your phone to establish an encrypted IPsec tunnel over your home Wi-Fi network back to your carrier's evolved Packet Data Gateway (ePDG). If your home Wi-Fi router's firewall blocks UDP Port 500 (IKE) or UDP Port 4500 (IPsec NAT-Traversal), the secure tunnel cannot form, preventing VoWiFi registration.

html:
You sit in your living room or office basement with zero cellular signal bars. You have a robust, high-speed 300 Mbps Wi-Fi connection, yet when someone dials your phone number, they hear: "The number you are calling is currently out of coverage area." Alternatively, you place an outgoing voice call over 4G LTE or 5G, only to watch your cellular icon abruptly drop to ancient 2G/3G, while your internet data freezes and the call audio turns robotic and muffled. In 2026, legacy circuit-switched cellular calling is obsolete. High-definition voice demands VoLTE (Voice over LTE) and VoWiFi (Voice over Wi-Fi). Here is the definitive telecommunications engineering guide to fixing registration failures and mastering carrier provisioning.

The Cellular Architecture of Modern Voice: What Is IMS?

In older 2G and 3G networks, voice calls and internet data traveled on completely separate physical pipelines: voice used dedicated, circuit-switched cellular frequencies, while data traveled over packet streams. When 4G LTE was engineered, telecommunications engineers eliminated circuit-switched voice entirely: 4G LTE and 5G are pure packet-data networks.

To transmit voice calls over high-speed packet networks, telecommunication carriers deployed the IP Multimedia Subsystem (IMS):

  • VoLTE (Voice over LTE): Converts your vocal cords into high-definition digital audio packets (encoded with the wideband AMR-WB or EVS codec) and streams them over prioritized LTE data channels with zero voice latency.
  • VoWiFi (Voice over Wi-Fi / Wi-Fi Calling): Uses your home or office Wi-Fi connection to establish an encrypted IPsec VPN tunnel directly into your cellular carrier's core IMS network (via the evolved Packet Data Gateway - ePDG). You can make and receive high-definition phone calls and SMS text messages with full clarity even in deep underground basements with zero cellular reception!

If VoLTE or VoWiFi fails, it means your device's operating system has failed to negotiate an authorized IMS Registration with your telecom provider.

Diagnostic 1: Checking Hidden IMS Service Status via the Secret '*#*#4636#*#*' Menu

Before modifying any settings, you must query your smartphone's baseband modem directly to see what the carrier network is reporting:

  1. Open the native Phone dialer app on your Android smartphone.
  2. Enter the universal Android diagnostic test code: *#*#4636#*#* (or *#*#4636#*#* on Pixel/Motorola/OnePlus; on Samsung devices, use *#0011# for ServiceMode).
  3. The hidden Testing menu will appear instantly. Tap on Phone information.
  4. Scroll through the technical parameters and inspect the hardware toggle switches:
    • VoLTE Provisioned: Must be toggled ON.
    • Wi-Fi Calling Provisioned: Must be toggled ON.
  5. Next, tap the three-dot menu icon (⋮) in the top right corner of the screen and select IMS Service Status.
  6. A system dialogue will appear displaying your real-time registration status:
    • IMS Registration: Registered (If it reads Unregistered, voice calling is broken!).
    • Voice over LTE: Available
    • Voice over Wi-Fi: Available

Diagnostic 2: Fixing Missing APN Bearer Configuration

An Access Point Name (APN) defines the network gateway pathway your phone uses to connect to your carrier's cellular data and IMS services. If you recently swapped SIM cards, updated your phone, or ported your mobile number, your phone may have fetched an incomplete generic APN profile that omits the dedicated IMS voice channel.

How to Reset and Reconfigure Carrier APNs:

  1. Navigate to Settings > Network & internet > SIMs (or Connections > Mobile networks > Access Point Names on Samsung).
  2. Select your active SIM card and tap Access Point Names.
  3. Tap the three-dot menu icon in the top right corner and select "Reset to default". This forces your phone to query your carrier's SIM card profile and reinstall certified network settings.
  4. Manual APN Verification: Tap on your active Internet APN to inspect its technical details:
    • Scroll down to APN type.
    • Ensure the field contains: default,supl,mms,ims,xcap. The presence of ims and xcap is mandatory for VoLTE and Wi-Fi calling routing!
    • Under APN protocol and APN roaming protocol, ensure both are set to IPv4/IPv6 (dual stack). Modern IMS packet voice fails if locked strictly to legacy IPv4.
    • Tap the three dots > Save. Toggle Airplane Mode on and off to establish a fresh network registration.

Diagnostic 3: Enabling Wi-Fi Calling (VoWiFi) Preferences in System Settings

Even when a smartphone is fully provisioned for VoWiFi, carrier software defaults to prioritizing cellular radio signals. If your phone detects even one faint, unusable bar of 2G or 4G signal, it may refuse to switch to Wi-Fi Calling unless explicitly commanded.

How to Configure Calling Preferences:

  1. Navigate to Settings > Network & internet > SIMs > [Your Carrier].
  2. Scroll down and locate Wi-Fi Calling.
  3. Toggle the master switch to ON.
  4. Tap on Calling preference:
    • Change the setting from "Call over mobile network" to "Call over Wi-Fi" (Wi-Fi Preferred).
    • Now, whenever your phone is connected to any trusted Wi-Fi network, it will immediately route all voice calls and SMS through Wi-Fi, completely eliminating indoor dead zones!
  5. Look at your status bar: within 10 seconds, a small phone handset icon with a Wi-Fi symbol (or the label "VoWiFi") will illuminate next to your signal bars.

Diagnostic 4: Resolving Home Wi-Fi Router Firewall IPsec Blocking (UDP 500 / 4500)

If your phone displays "VoWiFi Available" on public Wi-Fi networks (like Starbucks or the office), but steadfastly refuses to work on your home Wi-Fi, your home broadband router's firewall is blocking the carrier's encrypted IPsec tunnel.

How to Unblock VoWiFi on Your Home Router:

  1. Log into your home Wi-Fi router's admin gateway (typically 192.168.1.1).
  2. Navigate to Security > Firewall > ALG (Application Layer Gateway).
  3. Locate the toggle for "IPsec Passthrough" and verify that it is set to Enabled.
  4. Ensure your router's firewall is NOT blocking outbound traffic on:
    • UDP Port 500 (IKE - Internet Key Exchange)
    • UDP Port 4500 (IPsec NAT-Traversal)
  5. VoWiFi requires these two specific ports to establish the cryptographic tunnel back to your carrier's core network. Once enabled, restart your router; your smartphone will instantly register for Wi-Fi calling!

The Carrier Provisioning Request: When Your Account Is Blocked

If you have verified that your phone hardware supports VoLTE, your APN is pristine, and your router firewall is open, but the *#*#4636#*#* menu still displays "VoLTE Provisioned: Grayed Out / Unregistered", the block resides on your carrier account billing profile.

When you switch from an older phone or insert a legacy physical SIM card, the carrier's automated subscriber database (HLR/HSS) may still flag your line as a non-VoLTE device. Contact your telecommunication provider's customer service (e.g., dial 198 or 199 in India for Jio/Airtel/Vi; dial 611 in the US). State the following technical request: "My phone supports VoLTE and VoWiFi, but my line is not registered on the IMS core. Please push an automated Over-The-Air (OTA) IMS provisioning update to my SIM card and verify that the VoLTE feature flag is enabled on my subscriber profile." Within 2 to 4 hours of the carrier updating their database, your phone will register on the IMS network permanently.

The Verdict: Crystal-Clear Voice Everywhere You Go

Experiencing dropped calls inside your home or watching your cellular connection drop to ancient 2G voice in 2026 is an unacceptable compromise. High-definition voice over packet networks is a mature, robust technology. By checking your hidden IMS Service status via diagnostic test codes, ensuring your APN profile contains the mandatory ims bearer tags, configuring Wi-Fi Calling to 'Wi-Fi Preferred', and opening IPsec UDP ports on your router, you can enjoy flawless, studio-quality phone calls in any environment.

Understanding IMS Registration Architecture and SIP Handshakes

To effectively troubleshoot persistent VoLTE and VoWiFi failures, it is essential to understand the underlying telecom architecture: the IP Multimedia Subsystem (IMS). Unlike traditional circuit-switched 2G and 3G networks where voice calls occupied dedicated radio frequency slots, VoLTE and VoWiFi treat human speech as high-priority real-time Voice-over-IP (VoIP) data packets encoded via AMR-WB (Adaptive Multi-Rate Wideband) or EVS (Enhanced Voice Services) codecs.

When you insert a SIM card or connect to a trusted Wi-Fi network, your phone's cellular baseband modem initiates an IMS Registration Handshake via the Session Initiation Protocol (SIP):

  1. SIP REGISTER: The phone transmits a registration request containing your SIM's International Mobile Subscriber Identity (IMSI) to the carrier's Proxy-Call Session Control Function (P-CSCF) server.
  2. AKA Authentication: The carrier responds with a cryptographic challenge (401 Unauthorized), which your physical SIM or eSIM processes using its embedded cryptographic secret keys to generate an authentication digest.
  3. 200 OK & IPSec Tunneling: Upon successful cryptographic verification, the carrier establishes two permanent bi-directional IPSec security tunnels, securing all voice and SMS packets against eavesdropping.

If your device firmware lacks the specific carrier bundle profiles for your telecom operator, this SIP registration handshake fails silently at Step 1, causing your phone to drop back to 2G/3G circuits or drop calls altogether. Manually reprovisioning IMS configurations or resetting network settings forces the baseband processor to rebuild its carrier parameter tables.

ePDG Gateways: Diagnosing Wi-Fi Calling Router Firewalls

When Wi-Fi Calling (VoWiFi) refuses to engage despite a strong 5 GHz home Wi-Fi connection, the blockage almost always resides in your home or office router firewall. For VoWiFi to function, your phone must establish an encrypted IPSec VPN tunnel directly to your cellular carrier's evolved Packet Data Gateway (ePDG).

This secure tunnel relies strictly on two network protocols that many restrictive enterprise, hotel, and residential firewalls inadvertently block:

  • IKEv2 (Internet Key Exchange version 2): Operates over UDP Port 500. Used for initial cryptographic parameter negotiation and mutual authentication.
  • IPSec NAT-Traversal (NAT-T): Operates over UDP Port 4500. Carries all encapsulated voice and video RTP data packets through your router's Network Address Translation (NAT) table.
  • IPSec ESP (Encapsulating Security Payload - Protocol 50): Required on non-NAT networks.

If you manage your Wi-Fi router, access its administrative dashboard and verify that IPSec Passthrough and PPTP/L2TP Passthrough are enabled under the ALG (Application Layer Gateway) settings. Additionally, ensure that outgoing UDP ports 500 and 4500 are not blocked by parental controls or firewall rules. Once these ports are unblocked, your phone will register with the carrier's ePDG within 5 seconds of connecting to Wi-Fi!
